phenomena.claim: This domain contributes no phenomena of its own: mathematical-foundational structures are not directly observed, and their empirical contact runs entirely through the physics domains that deploy them
phenomena.source: constitutive scope statement for this record; every OBSERVED entry in the corpus lives in the ten physics-domain records (rrp/corpus/domains/)
phenomena.caveat: this is the evasion/reconstruction inventory named in RRP_00_REQUIREMENTS_PICTURE_01 section 7 (tranche-2 completeness layer)

formalism.claim: The domain's own formalism is the representation/uniqueness-theorem method: structural hypotheses in, uniqueness or classification out (Gleason, Soler, Stone-von Neumann, Wigner, the operational reconstructions all share this shape)
formalism.source: shape read off the individually verified theorem entries in this record (fetches of 2026-09-23 recorded per entry)
formalism.caveat: each theorem's output is conditional on its input structure; nothing in the method certifies that a physical system instantiates the hypotheses

formalism.claim: The lattice frame: the closed subspaces of a Hilbert space form an orthocomplemented (orthomodular) non-distributive lattice -- the 'quantum logic' arena in which Gleason and Soler operate
formalism.source: Birkhoff & von Neumann, 'The Logic of Quantum Mechanics', Ann. Math. 37, 823-843 (1936) -- bibliographic record verified 2026-09-23 (Cambridge Core / Annals listings)
formalism.caveat: the lattice is abstracted FROM the Hilbert-space formalism; taking it as a starting point for reconstruction is a separate move whose extra premises are recorded under primitives

primitives.claim: Gleason's theorem consumes as primitives: the projection lattice of a separable Hilbert space of dimension >= 3, and a noncontextual countably-additive probability assignment on it -- neither is derived by the theorem
primitives.source: Gleason, 'Measures on the closed subspaces of a Hilbert space', J. Math. Mech. 6(4), 885-893 (1957) -- record verified 2026-09-23 (IUMJ full-text listing; problem posed by Mackey; separable real or complex Hilbert space, dim >= 3)
primitives.caveat: noncontextuality (the measure depends on the projection alone, not the measurement context containing it) is the load-bearing physical assumption smuggled in as mathematics

primitives.claim: Soler's theorem consumes as primitives: an infinite-dimensional orthomodular space over a *-division ring containing an infinite orthonormal sequence -- the orthonormal-sequence hypothesis is what forces the classical field and it is an input, not physics
primitives.source: Soler, 'Characterization of Hilbert spaces by orthomodular spaces', Comm. Algebra 23(1), 219-243 (1995) -- bibliographic record verified 2026-09-23 (Taylor & Francis listing); role of the hypothesis per the surrounding literature (Holland, Bull. AMS 32 (1995))
primitives.caveat: finite-dimensional orthomodular spaces escape the theorem entirely; exotic infinite-dimensional orthomodular spaces (Keller spaces) are exactly what the hypothesis excludes

primitives.claim: The operational reconstructions (Hardy; Chiribella-D'Ariano-Perinotti) consume the operational framework itself as primitive: finite-dimensional systems, tests/outcomes, composition rules, and axioms such as local tomography or purification are inputs, not outputs
primitives.source: cross-reference: information_theory.json alternative_formulations (Hardy quant-ph/0101012; Chiribella-D'Ariano-Perinotti PRA 84, 012311 (2011); both abstract-verified there 2026-09-23) -- not duplicated here
primitives.caveat: bears on core item A (RRP_00_REQUIREMENTS_PICTURE_01 section 2.A): the composite-system axiom is where the subsystem/tensor structure enters as a declared input rather than being derived; see known_disconnects

derived_objects.claim: Gleason's theorem: on a separable real or complex Hilbert space of dimension >= 3, every countably-additive measure on the closed subspaces is of the form mu(P) = Tr(rho P) for a density operator rho -- the Born-rule FORM is derived from noncontextual probability structure on the given lattice
derived_objects.source: Gleason, J. Math. Mech. 6(4), 885-893 (1957) -- record verified 2026-09-23; adversarial re-fetch of the IUMJ abstract PDF p.885 (2026-09-23): exact wording is 'every measure on the closed subspaces is derived in this fashion', the fashion being mu(A) = trace(T P_A) with T a positive semi-definite self-adjoint trace-class operator (an earlier paraphrase was mistakenly set in quotation marks -- de-quoted here); issue number: the IUMJ database records 6(4) while the original print masthead reads Vol. 6 No. 6 -- both circulate; author/title/volume/pages/year exact
derived_objects.caveat: what it does NOT do: it presupposes the Hilbert lattice rather than deriving it; it does not select single-run outcomes; it fails in dimension 2; bears on core item D(ii) (RRP_00_REQUIREMENTS_PICTURE_01 section 2.D): it constrains the form of any noncontextual probability rule given the quantum frame but does not discharge the operational-probability priced input

derived_objects.claim: POVM-Gleason extension: probability assignments on effects (POVM elements) are of density-operator form in ALL dimensions including 2, by elementary arguments (Busch; Caves-Fuchs-Manne-Renes frame functions, including rational vector spaces)
derived_objects.source: Busch, 'Quantum states and generalized observables: a simple proof of Gleason's theorem', Phys. Rev. Lett. 91, 120403 (2003), quant-ph/9909073; Caves, Fuchs, Manne & Renes, 'Gleason-type derivations of the quantum probability rule for generalized measurements', Found. Phys. 34, 193 (2004), quant-ph/0306179 -- both arXiv abstracts fetched 2026-09-23
derived_objects.caveat: the gain in scope is bought by a strictly stronger premise: noncontextuality over ALL effects, not just projections -- a larger assumption about what counts as measurement

derived_objects.claim: Soler's theorem: an infinite-dimensional orthomodular space with an infinite orthonormal sequence is a classical Hilbert space over R, C, or the quaternions -- the number field is pinned to three candidates by lattice-theoretic structure
derived_objects.source: Soler, Comm. Algebra 23(1), 219-243 (1995) -- bibliographic record verified 2026-09-23
derived_objects.caveat: it does not select C over R or H (that selection needs further input, e.g. dynamics/Wigner-theorem considerations); together with Gleason it closes the quantum-logic reconstruction chain only up to those residues and only given the lattice frame

derived_objects.claim: Stone-von Neumann theorem: for finitely many degrees of freedom, all irreducible strongly-continuous unitary representations of the exponentiated (Weyl) canonical commutation relations are unitarily equivalent -- the Schrodinger representation is unique in its class
derived_objects.source: von Neumann, 'Die Eindeutigkeit der Schrodingerschen Operatoren', Math. Ann. 104, 570-578 (1931), doi:10.1007/BF01457956 -- record verified 2026-09-23 (Springer/EuDML listings; Rosenberg, 'A Selective History of the Stone-von Neumann Theorem' confirms attribution chain with Stone 1930)
derived_objects.caveat: uniqueness is scoped to finitely many degrees of freedom, Weyl (exponentiated) form, and strong continuity; each scope condition fails somewhere physical -- see limits and known_disconnects

empirical_inputs.claim: The domain consumes no empirical inputs: every theorem here is mathematics conditional on structural hypotheses; empirical content enters only where a physics domain identifies its structures with those hypotheses
empirical_inputs.source: constitutive scope statement; the identification steps live in the deploying records (e.g. quantum_mechanics.json formalism)

limits.claim: Stone-von Neumann uniqueness FAILS for infinitely many degrees of freedom: quantum field theory and the thermodynamic limit admit continua of unitarily inequivalent representations of the canonical commutation relations
limits.source: standard consequence recorded across the Haag's-theorem literature: Haag, Dan. Mat. Fys. Medd. 29(12), 1-37 (1955); Hall & Wightman, Dan. Mat. Fys. Medd. 31(5), 1-41 (1957); Earman & Fraser, 'Haag's Theorem and its Implications for the Foundations of Quantum Field Theory', Erkenntnis 64, 305 (2006) -- bibliographic records verified 2026-09-23 (Springer/philsci listings)
limits.caveat: the failure is of the theorem's finitely-many-degrees-of-freedom hypothesis, not an inconsistency; representation choice becomes physical data in the infinite case (cross-ref quantum_gravity_approaches.json type-III_1 entry for where this lands in AQFT)

known_disconnects.claim: Gleason's theorem does NOT select outcomes, does NOT derive the Hilbert lattice it operates on, and does NOT cover dimension 2 in its projective form; noncontextuality is assumed, not derived
known_disconnects.source: scope read off the verified Gleason record (J. Math. Mech. 6, 885 (1957), verified 2026-09-23); dim-2 gap and its POVM repair per Caves et al., Found. Phys. 34, 193 (2004), fetched 2026-09-23
known_disconnects.caveat: bears on core item D(ii) (RRP_00_REQUIREMENTS_PICTURE_01 section 2.D): the operational probability rule remains consumed-not-produced even with Gleason on the books -- the theorem shapes the rule given the frame; it does not produce outcomes or weights from dynamics

known_disconnects.claim: Haag's theorem: in an exact Poincare-covariant QFT with a unique vacuum, a field unitarily equivalent to a free field at one time is free at all times -- the interaction picture does not exist under the stated hypotheses
known_disconnects.source: Haag, 'On quantum field theories', Dan. Mat. Fys. Medd. 29(12), 1-37 (1955); generalized by Hall & Wightman, Dan. Mat. Fys. Medd. 31(5), 1-41 (1957); modern assessment Earman & Fraser, Erkenntnis 64, 305 (2006) -- bibliographic records verified 2026-09-23
known_disconnects.caveat: scope carefully: the theorem's hypotheses include exact covariance and a shared representation; regularized theories (finite volume, cutoffs) escape those hypotheses, which is how renormalized perturbation theory proceeds in practice -- the disconnect is between the exact axioms and the perturbative apparatus, not a refutation of the latter's approximation status

known_disconnects.claim: No reconstruction theorem on record selects the tensor-product/subsystem structure itself: Gleason and Soler presuppose the lattice of ONE system; the operational reconstructions take the composite-system rule (e.g. local tomography) as an axiom; which factorization is physical is input everywhere in this domain
known_disconnects.source: scope read off the verified reconstruction records in this file and in information_theory.json (fetches of 2026-09-23); cross-reference: quantum_mechanics.json primitives CPR entry (Cotler-Penington-Ranard uniqueness-given-existence, arXiv:1702.06142)
known_disconnects.caveat: bears on core item A (RRP_00_REQUIREMENTS_PICTURE_01 section 2.A): this absence is the mathematical-foundations face of the derive-or-price disjunction -- recorded here as what is absent, with CPR's conditional uniqueness as the standing partial result; no requirement asserted

known_disconnects.claim: No theorem in this domain derives the Standard Model gauge group SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1) or its representation content: group-theoretic classification (Lie theory, anomaly conditions) constrains what CAN be written down, never which structure is instantiated
known_disconnects.source: cross-reference: gauge_theory.json open_problems ('SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1) and its matter assignments are input everywhere; no audited framework derives them', verified there); classification-vs-selection split read off the verified Wigner-classification entry (quantum_field_theory_eft.json)
known_disconnects.caveat: bears on core items A and D (RRP_00_REQUIREMENTS_PICTURE_01 section 2): the gauge content sits on the priced-input side of every audited route, and nothing in the mathematical-foundations inventory moves it to the derived side; the anomaly-freedom consistency condition (core item C) constrains without fixing

open_problems.claim: No rigorous interacting 4D quantum field theory has been constructed (Yang-Mills existence and mass gap open): the mathematical foundation of the empirically most successful framework is incomplete
open_problems.source: cross-reference: quantum_mechanics.json limits caveat ('no rigorous interacting 4D construction -- recorded second-order gap, RAI_STRUCTURAL_THEORY_SEARCH section 8', verified there); constructive-QFT status is community-standard
open_problems.caveat: Clay Millennium problem statement (Jaffe & Witten) named as the Stage-2 primary-citation target; the gap coexists with the framework's precision success -- it is a foundations gap, not an empirical one

open_problems.claim: No extension of the reconstruction-theorem program (Gleason/Soler/operational axioms) to infinite-dimensional systems, QFT, or gravity is on record
open_problems.source: cross-reference: information_theory.json open_problems ('No extension of the informational reconstruction theorems beyond finite-dimensional operational theories... is on record', verified there 2026-09-23); Soler covers infinite-dimensional single systems but not composition or dynamics
open_problems.caveat: an extension covering subsystem structure would bear directly on core item A; none exists at this record's date

alternative_formulations.source: cross-reference: information_theory.json alternative_formulations entries 1-3 (Hardy quant-ph/0101012; CDP PRA 84, 012311 (2011); CBH Found. alternative_formulations.claim: Categorical/process-theoretic formulation: quantum mechanics and its protocols recast in compact closed categories with biproducts, with scalars and the Born rule emerging from the categorical structure
alternative_formulations.source: Abramsky & Coecke, 'A categorical semantics of quantum protocols', Proc. 19th IEEE LiCS (2004), quant-ph/0402130 -- arXiv abstract fetched 2026-09-23
alternative_formulations.caveat: a reformulation and abstraction of the existing formalism, not an independent derivation of it; teleportation/entanglement-swapping protocols are its verification cases

domain_of_validity.claim: Every theorem in this record holds exactly under its stated hypotheses and nowhere else is anything claimed: projective Gleason needs dim >= 3 and separability; POVM-Gleason needs effect-noncontextuality; Soler needs infinite dimension with an orthonormal sequence; Stone-von Neumann needs finitely many degrees of freedom, Weyl form, strong continuity; the operational reconstructions need finite dimension. The physical reach of each is exactly the fidelity of the identification between a physics domain's structures and these hypotheses
domain_of_validity.source: boundary assembled from the individually verified entries above (fetch dates 2026-09-23 recorded per entry)
domain_of_validity.caveat: the identification steps themselves are physics-domain content and carry their own provenance in the sibling records
